To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electromagnetic transition strengths observed in the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain up to (216)Lb are described by a new shell-model Hamiltonian that incorporates the effective three-body force and a two-body transition operator.

(a) new isomers have been discovered in (212-216)Pb and their electromagnetic properties have been measured; (b) the experimental results cannot be explained within a shell model framework; (c) a microscopic effective interaction, based on a realistic three-body interaction, is able to describe the experimental results.
the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain up to (216)Lb has been studied for the rst time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of nuclear structure phenomena in the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain.

the study of the full seniority structure of the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain, up to neutron number N = 126, and with the investigation of its impact on the description of the nuclear structure of these nuclei, in particular on the electromagnetic transition rates.
the description of exotic nuclear structures and the development of a microscopic description of the underlying forces in terms of nucleon-nucleon interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shell model with effective two- and three-body forces is a successful tool to describe the low-lying states of the neutron-rich Pb isotopes.

effective three-body interactions are needed to explain the electromagnetic properties of the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain, and that they are not yet fully accounted for in current effective interaction models.

the experimental results are consistent with a description of the lead isotopes within the framework of the shell model with the addition of effective three-body interaction and two-body transition operator in the conventional neutron single particle space beyond (208), and that the experimental results do not support a description within the framework of a simple two-neutron halo model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new class of isomeric states has been found in the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain.
the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain has been extended by 8 neutron-rich nuclei.
the neutron-rich lead isotopic chain is an excellent testing ground for the nuclear shell model and its extensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isomeric states in neutron-rich lead isotopic chain are not well described by the shell model with the standard two-body effective interactions.
the neutron-rich Pb isotopes provide a new testing ground for effective interactions beyond the conventional valence space.

the description of the electromagnetic transition strengths in the neutron-rich Pb isotopes requires an effective three-body interaction in order to account for the large deformation of the ground states and the large collectivity of the excited states.
